title: UK GDP monthly estimate, October 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the last UK activity read the December MPC sees, and the month that carries most of the Q4 nowcast
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpmonthlyestimateukoctober2026, fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'GDP monthly estimate, UK: October 2026', 'Release date: 11 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published'. A plain 'Release date', not the 'Provisional release date' the ONS puts on its quarterly-estimate pages, so the slot is firm on the publisher's own labelling. Filed estimate on two counts only: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics, and this lane does not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The date itself is not labelled provisional by anyone
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-gdp-monthly-2027-01-15 LANE, 2026-09-10, during that event's never-assessed initial research. Proposed because it is the PRIOR STATE in that lane's central measurement and the measurement is not readable without it. The proposing ledger reconstructs what a Q4 q/q read is worth at each stage across eleven post-2013 ex-COVID Q4s (ONS 4dp workbook monthlygdpto4dp.xlsx, fetched direct 2026-09-10): R2 = -0.561 / MAE 0.332pp before any Q4 monthly data, R2 = +0.549 / MAE 0.161pp once OCTOBER is known, R2 = +0.810 / MAE 0.124pp once November is known. This release is the middle rung — it is where most of the Q4 information arrives, and the 2027-01-15 November print is the confirmation on top of it. TWO FURTHER REASONS IT EARNS ITS OWN SLOT. It is the LAST UK GDP read before the Bank of England's 2026-12-17 announcement, which its upcoming-MPC-dates page (fetched direct 2026-09-10) lists under '2026 confirmed dates' as 'Thursday 17 December — December MPC Summary and minutes'. And it is this calendar's own watch trigger: the proposing ledger's only horizon graded above stand-aside is 'This quarter — watch', and what is being watched is precisely whether THIS print lands outside +/-0.40pp (2 of 11 post-2013 ex-COVID Octobers did), which would make the January print a genuine swing factor rather than a confirmation. October is also the second-widest month of the twelve in this series (m/m sd 0.396pp against November's 0.195pp), so a large print here is materially more likely than a large one there. The proposing lane makes NO claim about this release's market impact: symbols is empty, no instrument script was run, and the LOW tier reflects the absence of a transmission path — the ten tracked names are all US-listed and a grep for gilt/sterling/GBP across trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md returns nothing. ID PREFIX NOTE: uk-gdp-monthly-* matches the canonical uk-gdp-monthly-2027-01-15.json written by the same lane on the same day and the uk-cpi-/uk-ppi-/uk-labour-market- convention; a sibling lane has a competing proposal for the same release family under the opposite uk-monthly-gdp-* prefix (proposals/uk-monthly-gdp-2026-10-15.from-uk-blue-book-2026-10-30.json), flagged in both places and not this lane's to rename or delete. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
